definitions.definition: Trespa is a brand of high-pressure laminate (HPL) panels, widely used in exterior building facades and cladding, and also in interior applications like countertops and toilet partitions. The best-known product line is Trespa Meteon, an exterior-grade panel made from wood-based fibres saturated with thermosetting resins, pressed under high heat and pressure, with a decorative surface layer (often using their ELP - Electron Beam Cured Acrylate - coating for extra weather and UV resistance).
key_characteristics: Weather resistant - designed to withstand UV, rain, frost and pollution without significant fading or degrading.
Low maintenance - does not need painting or sealing like wood.
Wide range of colours and finishes - including wood-look, stone-look and solid colours.
Used for rainscreen cladding, balcony panels, fencing, signage and facade systems on commercial and residential buildings.
definitions.background: It is a Dutch company (part of the Hexion/Trespa International group), well known in architecture and construction circles across Europe.
definitions.afterfade_context: Trespa panels are typically a compact laminate, not aluminium or PVC, so Afterfade Pro-Tech+ is not intended or tested for that surface. If a customer asks about using it on Trespa cladding, treat it as falling outside the tested surface range: flag it for a test-patch-and-caution answer, or escalate if precision matters.

definitions.definition: A door wreath is a circular (or otherwise shaped) arrangement of decorative materials hung on a front or interior door, usually as seasonal decoration. Wreaths are made from a wide range of materials: plastic or resin, metal wire, painted wood, fabric, and natural or dried plant material such as pine, eucalyptus, branches and leaves. Common types include Christmas wreaths, autumn wreaths and year-round welcome wreaths.
key_characteristics: Decorative, not structural - hung on the door and not exposed to the same wear as windows, doors, gates or shutters.
Materials vary widely, so surface suitability depends on what the wreath is actually made of.
Often mounted on the outside of the door, where it is exposed to sun, rain, frost and wind.
Plastic, resin, painted metal and painted wood wreaths are the material types that could potentially be treated; natural or dried plant material cannot.
definitions.background: Door wreaths are a traditional decoration in many European markets and a common autumn/winter product, particularly around Christmas.
definitions.afterfade_context: A door wreath is not a surface Afterfade markets or tests for. If a customer asks about restoring a faded plastic, resin, painted metal or painted wood wreath, treat it like any other surface outside the core aluminium and PVC range: it can be used with a test patch on a small hidden area first, and no specific result or lifespan should be promised. Never recommend Afterfade Pro-Tech+ for natural or dried plant material, fabric, or anything a customer would not treat as a coated surface.
